discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism, but the particle itself was found by experimenters, and that half of the story is still unrecognised. Peter Jenni, founding spokesperson of ATLAS, and Tejinder Virdee, a founder and leading architect of CMS, conceived and built detectors of unprecedented scale and precision. Fabiola Gianotti led ATLAS through the 2012 discovery. Their July 2012 observation of a scalar near 125 GeV, with independent confirmation from two experiments, was the first discovery of a fundamental spin-zero particle. Later measurements of its couplings confirmed that it gives mass to the W and Z bosons and to fermions. The discovery completed the Standard Model and made the hierarchy problem, the question of why the Higgs mass is so light, a concrete experimental question. It opens a new era in which the Higgs sector is a precision probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. Experiment is the final arbiter, and this achievement deserves recognition.
